summary: GPDO 2015 (SI 2015/596) Sch.2 Part 1 analysis for 115 Vicarage Road (detached, hipped roof). (1) PD ENVELOPE: (a) Class A.1(g) allows a single-storey rear enlargement extending "beyond the rear wall of the original dwellinghouse by more than 4 metres... up to 8 metres in the case of a detached dwellinghouse" subject to the A.4 neighbour-consultation prior approval. The 8m is measured from the ORIGINAL (as-built or as at 1.7.1948) rear wall and, critically, A.1(ja) provides that "any total enlargement (being the enlarged part together with any existing enlargement of the original dwellinghouse to which it will be joined) exceeds or would exceed the limits set out in sub-paragraphs (e) to (j)" takes the scheme outside Class A — so the 2005 ~3.3m extension does NOT need demolition: it can be retained and extended, but existing (3.3m) + new must total no more than 8m from the original rear wall, and the JOINED total must also comply with the 4m height and 3m-eaves-within-2m-of-boundary limits (A.1(f)(ii)/(i)). If the retained extension itself breaches any (e)-(j) limit when assessed as part of the total, PD is lost — so verify the 2005 extension's height/eaves and check the 2005 permission for PD-removing conditions (GPDO art.3(4); Dunnett Investments [2017] EWCA Civ 192 requires clear express words to exclude the GPDO). (b) Two-storey rear under A.1(h): the enlarged part with "more than one storey" must not "extend beyond the rear wall of the original dwellinghouse by more than 3 metres" nor "be within 7 metres of any boundary... opposite the rear wall"; conditions A.3(b) (obscure-glazed, non-opening-below-1.7m upper side windows) and A.3(c) (roof pitch of any multi-storey enlarged part must "so far as practicable" match the original — i.e. hipped to match). NOTE: there is no "10.5m/7m side rule" in Class A — the side-elevation limits are in A.1(j) (single storey, max 4m height, max half the width of the original dwellinghouse); do not rely on a 10.5m figure. Combining the 3m two-storey with the 8m single-storey run in one joined structure is high-risk under A.1(ja)/(g) (the larger-home right applies only where the enlarged part "would have a single storey") — sequence or sever them, or take the two-storey element through planning (the pre-app already concedes 4m two-storey, which beats the 3m PD right). (c) Class AA (inserted by SI 2020/755): "up to two additional storeys, where the existing dwellinghouse consists of two or more storeys... immediately above the topmost storey", not permitted if constructed before 1.7.1948 or after 28.10.2018, if the resulting height would "exceed 18 metres", if it would exceed the existing roof height by more than 7m (two storeys)/3.5m (one), or if "the floor to ceiling height of any additional storey, measured internally, would exceed the lower of (i) 3 metres or (ii) the floor to ceiling height, measured internally, of any storey of the principal part of the existing dwellinghouse". Storeys must sit on the "principal part" (main house excluding any single-storey front/side/rear extensions) — so NOT over the rear extension; the flat-roofed two-storey side wing is also outside the principal part. Prior approval (amenity incl. overlooking/privacy/loss of light, and external appearance) is mandatory, development cannot begin before approval is granted, and works must be "completed within a period of 3 years" of the prior approval; conditions include NO windows in any side elevation wall/roof slope and the roof pitch of the principal part must match the existing (hipped — consistent with the officer's demand). (d) Class B: enlargement of the roof up to "50 cubic metres in any other case [than a terrace]" measured against the ORIGINAL roof space; B.3 defines "resulting roof space" as "the roof space as enlarged, taking into account any enlargement to the original roof space, whether permitted by this Class or not". Since the 25 May 2024 amendment (SI 2024/579), B.2(b) expressly contemplates "an enlargement which joins the original roof to the roof of a rear or side extension" (exempting it from the 0.2m eaves set-back and the original-external-wall limits) — statutory recognition that an L-shaped dormer can sit over an extension roof, provided nothing exceeds "the height of the highest part of the existing roof" (B.1(a)) and nothing passes the principal-elevation roof plane. Caveat: appeal decisions on dormers over NON-original projections remain mixed; the 50m³ counts ALL roof additions cumulatively, and doing Class AA first exhausts/negates Class B (and vice-versa consumes nothing from AA — choose AA storeys OR B dormers on the main roof; on a hipped detached house, hip-to-gable plus rear dormer within 50m³ is the classic Class B maximiser but conflicts with the 'match the hipped roof' merits position if a planning application is also pending). (e) Side: A.1(j) — beyond a side wall of the original house only single storey, ≤4m high, width ≤ half the original house's width; the existing two-storey side wing already uses side massing and counts within any joined "total enlargement" under (ja). (2) SEQUENCING: It is entirely lawful to secure the 8m prior approval (and build or not) FIRST, then apply for planning permission for a first floor above/behind it; the LPA cannot refuse the prior approval on design/subservience/SPD grounds — under A.4 it may assess ONLY "the impact of the proposed development on the amenity of any adjoining premises" (and only if an adjoining owner objects within 21 days; silence for 42 days = deemed ability to proceed). The extant prior approval/LDC then operates as a fallback material consideration in the planning application: Mansell v Tonbridge & Malling BC [2017] EWCA Civ 1314 (Lindblom LJ, [27]): for a fallback "the prospect does not have to be probable or likely: a 'real prospect' will suffice" — a granted prior approval plus demonstrated intent (or a started build) is a paradigm real prospect, pressuring the LPA to accept the officer's conceded 4m two-storey over an 8m ground floor rather than force a worse PD outcome. Building a planning-permission extension does NOT extinguish PD rights generally, BUT (i) art.3(4): "Nothing in this Order permits development contrary to any condition imposed by any planning permission granted or deemed to be granted under Part 3 of the Act otherwise than by this Order" — check the 2005 and any new permission for PD-restricting conditions (and resist/negotiate any such condition on the new two-storey consent, since Birmingham could use one to sterilise the remaining PD stack); and (ii) anything built under planning permission still counts against the PD arithmetic (it is not "original", feeds A.1(ja) totals and the 50% cap). Order of play that maximises massing: 1. LDC/s.192 audit of the 2005 permission conditions; 2. Class A prior approval for full-width single-storey rear to 8m total (retaining/subsuming the 2005 extension), leaning on the pre-app concession that the 45-degree code runs from the END of No.117's solid-walled conservatory (which projects 60cm beyond 115's existing extension) — a pure amenity test the site appears to pass; 3. planning application for the 4m-deep two-storey rear element (hipped roof to match) with the 8m fallback pleaded via Mansell; 4. Class AA prior approval OR Class B (hip-to-gable + rear/L dormer, 50m³) on the principal part — mutually exclusive in practice because B.3 counts AA volume against B's original-roof-space baseline; 5. Class A.1(j) single-storey side infill if width headroom remains. (3) 50% CAP — A.1(b): development is not permitted if "the total area of ground covered by buildings within the curtilage of the dwellinghouse (other than the original dwellinghouse) would exceed 50% of the total area of the curtilage (excluding the ground area of the original dwellinghouse)". Arithmetic: Numerator = ground footprint of ALL buildings other than the original house — the 2005 rear extension, any post-1948 ground coverage of the side wing, all sheds/garages/outbuildings, plus the proposed works; Denominator = total curtilage area MINUS the original house's footprint. Both PD and planning-permission extensions count in the numerator; demolishing an outbuilding frees headroom. A site survey with the original 1930s(?) footprint is needed to run the numbers — flagged as an open question. (4) s.192 LDCs: under s.192(1)-(2) TCPA 1990 the LPA "shall" issue a certificate if satisfied the described operations "would be lawful if... begun at the time of the application", and s.192(4) makes lawfulness "conclusively presumed unless there is a material change, before... the operations are begun, in any of the matters relevant to determining such lawfulness". Use s.192 to make the two-storey-3m fallback, side extension and Class B elements incontestable BEFORE the planning application (maximum Mansell leverage). CAVEAT: an LDC cannot ordinarily be granted for the A.1(g) larger-home extension until the A.4 prior-approval procedure has run (the development is not yet lawful without it); certify that element after prior approval, or via s.191 once built. Each LDC also freezes the position against any future Article 4 direction or GPDO amendment (subject to s.192(4)'s material-change proviso).

facts.topic: Class A.1(g) larger home extension (detached)
facts.detail: Development is not permitted by Class A if (for a house not on article 2(3) land or an SSSI) the enlarged part would have a single storey and extend beyond the rear wall of the original dwellinghouse by more than 8 metres in the case of a detached dwellinghouse (6m any other), or exceed 4 metres in height. The 8m is measured from the ORIGINAL rear wall, and applies to the TOTAL enlargement where joined to an existing extension (see A.1(ja)). Subject to the A.4 prior approval (neighbour consultation) procedure.
facts.value: 8m from original rear wall, single storey, max 4m high, prior approval required
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/schedule/2/part/1 (Class A, para A.1(g))

facts.topic: Class A.1(ja) — existing 2005 extension need NOT be demolished
facts.detail: Verbatim: development is not permitted if "any total enlargement (being the enlarged part together with any existing enlargement of the original dwellinghouse to which it will be joined) exceeds or would exceed the limits set out in sub-paragraphs (e) to (j)". Effect: the 2005 ~3.3m extension can be retained and extended to a combined 8m from the original rear wall, provided the joined TOTAL also complies with every limit in (e)-(j) (height ≤4m, eaves ≤3m within 2m of a boundary, etc.). If the retained extension breaches any limit as part of the total, Class A is lost entirely for the joined enlargement.
facts.value: A.1(ja) — limits apply to total enlargement, refs sub-paras (e) to (j)
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/schedule/2/part/1; cross-checked via search of consolidated text and Planning Jungle commentary

facts.topic: Class A.1(f) standard rear limit
facts.detail: Verbatim (per legislation.gov.uk snippet): "subject to paragraph (g), the enlarged part of the dwellinghouse would have a single storey and—(i) extend beyond the rear wall of the original dwellinghouse by more than 4 metres in the case of a detached dwellinghouse, or 3 metres in the case of any other dwellinghouse, or (ii) exceed 4 metres in height".
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/schedule/2/part/1 Class A.1(f)

facts.topic: Class A.1(h) two-storey rear — 3m and 7m rules
facts.detail: The enlarged part with more than one storey must not (i) extend beyond the rear wall of the original dwellinghouse by more than 3 metres, or (ii) be within 7 metres of any boundary of the curtilage opposite the rear wall. Measure 115's rear garden depth: if the rear boundary is closer than 7m to the proposed two-storey back wall, the PD two-storey right fails and the planning route (4m conceded at pre-app) is the only two-storey option.
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/schedule/2/part/1 Class A.1(h)

facts.topic: No '10.5m/7m side rule' exists in Class A
facts.detail: The task's reference to '10.5m/7m side rules' does not correspond to any Class A provision. The side-elevation limits are A.1(j): an enlarged part extending beyond a wall forming a side elevation of the original dwellinghouse must not exceed 4 metres in height, have more than a single storey, or have a width greater than half the width of the original dwellinghouse. The only 7m rule is the rear-boundary rule in A.1(h)(ii); 3.5m/7m height uplifts belong to Class AA.
facts.value: A.1(j): single storey, ≤4m high, ≤half original width
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/schedule/2/part/1 Class A.1(j)

facts.topic: Class A.1(i) eaves near boundary
facts.detail: Development not permitted if the enlarged part is within 2 metres of the boundary of the curtilage and the height of the eaves of the enlarged part would exceed 3 metres. Relevant on the No.117 side (78cm gap to the conservatory) and the No.113 alley side (125cm gap) — the 8m extension's eaves must stay at or below 3m along those flanks.
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/schedule/2/part/1 Class A.1(i)

facts.topic: Class A.3 conditions
facts.detail: (a) exterior materials of similar appearance to the existing house; (b) any upper-floor window in a wall or roof slope forming a side elevation must be obscure-glazed and non-opening unless the opening parts are more than 1.7m above the floor; (c) where the enlarged part has more than one storey, its roof pitch must so far as practicable be the same as that of the original dwellinghouse — i.e. a PD two-storey rear must carry a hipped-matching pitch, aligning with the officer's 'match the existing hipped roof' merits position.
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/schedule/2/part/1 Class A.3

facts.topic: A.4 prior approval mechanics — amenity-only test
facts.detail: The developer submits a written description and plan; the LPA notifies adjoining owners/occupiers who have 21 days to object. Only if an objection is made must the LPA assess — and it may assess ONLY — "the impact of the proposed development on the amenity of any adjoining premises". Design, subservience, Birmingham Design Guide SPD and 'overdevelopment' are NOT lawful grounds of refusal at prior approval. Development may begin on receipt of written notice that prior approval is not required, on receipt of prior approval, or on expiry of 42 days without any LPA determination. The developer must notify the LPA on completion (as soon as reasonably practicable).
facts.value: 21-day neighbour window; 42-day deemed right to proceed; amenity-only assessment
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/schedule/2/part/1 Class A.4; planningjungle.com Larger Rear Extensions guide

facts.topic: 45-degree code concession applies at prior approval
facts.detail: Birmingham applies its 45 Degree Code as its amenity yardstick in larger-home-extension prior approvals. The pre-app (2026/03356/PA) records in writing that the code is taken from the END of No.117's solid-walled conservatory (which projects 60cm beyond 115's existing extension) rather than from window openings, and that the code 'would appear to be met from both neighbouring properties'. That written concession is strong evidence that an amenity-based objection under A.4 should fail, making the 8m (or the maximum depth that still clears the 45-degree line from No.113's window centre 180cm from the extension corner) prior approval highly defensible.
facts.source: Pre-app response 2026/03356/PA (Leah Russell MRTPI, Birmingham CC), provided in task

facts.topic: Class AA scope (verbatim key limits)
facts.detail: Permits "up to two additional storeys, where the existing dwellinghouse consists of two or more storeys" (one storey if single-storey house), "immediately above the topmost storey of the dwellinghouse", plus reasonably necessary engineering operations. Not permitted if the house was constructed before 1 July 1948 or after 28 October 2018; if the resulting height of the highest part would "exceed 18 metres"; if it would exceed the existing roof height by more than 3.5m (one storey added) or 7m (two storeys); or if "the floor to ceiling height of any additional storey, measured internally, would exceed the lower of (i) 3 metres, or (ii) the floor to ceiling height, measured internally, of any storey of the principal part of the existing dwellinghouse". Additional storeys must be on the 'principal part' — the main part of the house EXCLUDING any single-storey front/side/rear extension (original or later) — so no AA storeys over the rear extension; the flat-roof two-storey side wing is also outside the principal part.
facts.value: Detached: ≤18m total, +7m max for 2 storeys, ≤3m internal per storey, principal part only
facts.source: SI 2020/755 inserting Class AA; legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2020/755/made; legislation.gov.uk Class AA crossheading

facts.topic: Class AA conditions and prior approval
facts.detail: Conditions: similar materials; NO window in any wall or roof slope forming a side elevation; the roof pitch of the principal part following development must be the same as the existing roof pitch (hipped stays hipped); C3 use retained. Prior approval application is mandatory and covers, inter alia, impact on amenity of adjoining premises (overlooking, privacy, loss of light) and the external appearance of the dwellinghouse; unlike Class A there is no 42-day deemed approval — development must not begin before prior approval is granted, and must be completed within 3 years of the grant.
facts.value: No side windows; matching pitch; 3-year completion; no deemed consent
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk Class AA paragraphs AA.2-AA.3; planninggeek.co.uk/gpdo/house/class-aa/; lichfields.uk analysis

facts.topic: Class B roof enlargement — 50 cubic metres
facts.detail: Class B permits enlargement of a dwellinghouse consisting of an addition or alteration to its roof. Not permitted if any part of the dwellinghouse would, as a result, exceed the height of the highest part of the existing roof (B.1(a)); extend beyond the plane of any existing roof slope forming the principal elevation fronting a highway (B.1(b)); or if "the cubic content of the resulting roof space would exceed the cubic content of the original roof space by more than (i) 40 cubic metres in the case of a terrace house, or (ii) 50 cubic metres in any other case" (B.1(d)). B.3 (interpretation): "'resulting roof space' means the roof space as enlarged, taking into account any enlargement to the original roof space, whether permitted by this Class or not" — the 50m³ is a cumulative once-only allowance for the property.
facts.value: 50 m³ (detached) vs ORIGINAL roof space, cumulative
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/schedule/2/part/1 Class B crossheading

facts.topic: Class B over a Class A extension roof (L-shaped dormer)
facts.detail: B.2(b) as amended now reads that the eaves set-back (edge of enlargement "so far as practicable, not less than 0.2 metres from the eaves, measured along the roof slope from the outside edge of the eaves") and the bar on extending beyond the outside face of any external wall of the original dwellinghouse apply "other than in the case of a hip-to-gable enlargement or an enlargement which joins the original roof to the roof of a rear or side extension" — i.e. the Order now expressly contemplates a roof enlargement (an L-shaped dormer) joining the main roof to the roof of a rear extension, including one built under Class A. Constraints remain: nothing above the highest part of the existing main roof (B.1(a)), nothing through the principal-elevation roof plane, all volume counted against the 50m³/original-roof-space test, side windows obscure-glazed. Caveat: pre-amendment appeal decisions on dormers over non-original projections were divided; obtain an s.192 LDC to settle it for this site.
facts.value: Expressly enabled by amended B.2(b); volume still capped at 50 m³
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk Class B (current consolidated); amendment understood to be SI 2024/579 in force 25 May 2024; khub.net PAS forum discussion of the change

facts.topic: Class AA vs Class B are practically mutually exclusive
facts.detail: Because B.3 counts ANY enlargement of the original roof space "whether permitted by this Class or not", adding Class AA storeys (which replace/raise the roof) exhausts the 50m³ Class B allowance; conversely a Class B dormer scheme reshapes the roof AA would build on and AA is excluded where the house has already been enlarged by an additional storey. Choose the bigger prize: AA gives up to two full storeys on the principal part (subject to external-appearance prior approval); B gives up to 50m³ of dormers including over the rear extension with no external-appearance discretion beyond the fixed conditions. For maximum massing on a two-storey detached within 18m, AA (up to +7m) normally beats B (50m³), but AA prior approval carries refusal risk on external appearance; B with hip-to-gable + rear/L dormer is the low-discretion route.
facts.source: Analysis of B.1(d)/B.3 and AA.1 interaction, both on legislation.gov.uk

facts.topic: 50% curtilage cap arithmetic (A.1(b))
facts.detail: Development not permitted if the total area of ground covered by buildings within the curtilage (other than the original dwellinghouse) would exceed 50% of the total area of the curtilage (excluding the ground area of the original dwellinghouse). Numerator: ground footprints of the 2005 rear extension, any post-1948 ground coverage under the side wing, garage(s), sheds and all outbuildings, PLUS the proposed enlargements (however consented — planning-permission extensions count too). Denominator: total curtilage minus the ORIGINAL house footprint. Extensions with planning permission still consume the cap; demolishing outbuildings restores headroom. Requires measured survey of curtilage and original footprint to compute for 115 Vicarage Road.
facts.value: Σ(non-original building footprints) ≤ 0.5 × (curtilage − original house footprint)
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/schedule/2/part/1 Class A.1(b); MHCLG Technical Guidance (Sept 2019)

facts.topic: 'Original' definition
facts.detail: Article 2(1) GPDO: 'original' means, in relation to a building existing on 1 July 1948, as existing on that date, and in relation to a building built on or after 1 July 1948, as so built. All Class A depth measurements at 115 run from the original rear/side walls, not from the 2005 extension; the two-storey side wing, if not original, is itself an 'existing enlargement' for A.1(ja) purposes when joined to new work.
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/article/2

facts.topic: Sequencing: prior-approval 8m first, then planning for first floor — lawful
facts.detail: Nothing in the GPDO or TCPA prevents securing (and building out) the A.1(g) 8m prior approval and then applying for planning permission for a first floor above part of it. The prior approval process cannot consider the future intention; the later planning application is determined on its merits with the lawful ground floor as the baseline. The officer has already conceded the principle of a two-storey rear at 4m depth — a planning application for a 4m-deep hipped two-storey element over/behind an 8m PD ground floor combines both maxima. Risk control: do not present the two elements as one integrated building operation at prior-approval stage (a 'contrived single operation' argument), and keep the two-storey element within the conceded 4m envelope.
facts.source: GPDO structure; Mansell v Tonbridge & Malling BC [2017] EWCA Civ 1314; pre-app 2026/03356/PA concession

facts.topic: Fallback weight — Mansell
facts.detail: Mansell v Tonbridge & Malling BC [2017] EWCA Civ 1314, Lindblom LJ at [27]: a fallback development is a material consideration where there is a 'real prospect' of it being carried out, and "for a prospect to be a real prospect, it does not have to be probable or likely: a possibility will suffice". An extant Class A prior approval (better: with an s.192 LDC and/or a commenced build) for the 8m extension, and an LDC for the 3m two-storey PD alternative, are classic fallbacks the LPA must weigh when determining the two-storey planning application — the argument being that refusal achieves a worse outcome for neighbours than the conceded 4m scheme.
facts.source: bailii.org/ew/cases/EWCA/Civ/2017/1314.html; midsussex.gov.uk CD12.18 copy of judgment

facts.topic: Does building a planning-permission extension extinguish PD rights?
facts.detail: No general extinguishment. Two qualifications: (1) GPDO article 3(4): "Nothing in this Order permits development contrary to any condition imposed by any planning permission granted or deemed to be granted under Part 3 of the Act otherwise than by this Order" — a PD-removing condition on the 2005 permission (check the decision notice) or on any new permission would bite, but per Dunnett Investments Ltd v SSCLG [2017] EWCA Civ 192 only clear and express words exclude the GPDO. Negotiate against any such condition on the new consent. (2) Arithmetical consumption: anything built (under permission or PD) is not 'original', counts within any A.1(ja) joined total, counts against the 50% cap, and changes the 'existing dwellinghouse/roof' baselines used by Classes AA and B.
facts.source: legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2015/596/article/3; Dunnett Investments [2017] EWCA Civ 192; localgovernmentlawyer.co.uk 'Permitted Development: pitfalls'

facts.topic: s.192 LDC — making each element incontestable
facts.detail: TCPA 1990 s.192(1)-(2): on an application describing proposed operations, if the LPA is provided with information satisfying them that the operations "would be lawful if instituted or begun at the time of the application, they shall issue a certificate to that effect; and in any other case they shall refuse" — a purely legal test, no planning judgment, appealable under s.195. s.192(4): "The lawfulness of any use or operations for which a certificate is in force under this section shall be conclusively presumed unless there is a material change, before the use is instituted or the operations are begun, in any of the matters relevant to determining such lawfulness." Strategy: obtain s.192 LDCs for (i) the 3m two-storey PD fallback, (ii) the A.1(j) side extension, (iii) the Class B roof scheme — before lodging the planning application, to lock in Mansell fallbacks and insulate against a future Article 4 direction (subject to the material-change proviso).
facts.source: TCPA 1990 s.192; MHCLG Annex 8 'Lawfulness and the LDC' (assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/5a78a10a40f0b62b22cbb850/321541.pdf)

facts.topic: s.192 limitation for the larger home extension
facts.detail: An A.1(g) 8m extension is only permitted development once the A.4 prior-approval procedure has been completed (approval granted, notice that approval not required, or 42 days' silence). Before that, the proposed operations 'would not be lawful if begun at the time of the application', so LPAs routinely refuse s.192 certificates for larger-home extensions applied for in advance of prior approval. Correct order: prior approval first, then (if belt-and-braces desired) s.192 relying on the completed procedure, or s.191 after build-out.
facts.source: GPDO A.4 read with TCPA 1990 s.192(2); Planning Jungle Class A (Larger Rear Extensions) guide

facts.topic: Pre-app design objections are irrelevant to the PD stack
facts.detail: The refusal reasoning in 2026/03356/PA (overdevelopment, subservience, Birmingham Design Guide SPD 2022, City Note LW-16, 'reduce to 4m') is merits policy that applies ONLY to the planning application. It cannot be applied to Class A prior approval (amenity-of-adjoining-premises only), to Class B (no prior approval at all — conditions only), or to the LDC tests (purely legal). Only Class AA prior approval imports 'external appearance' as a discretionary matter. The maximum-massing strategy therefore routes everything except the 4m two-storey element around the Design Guide.
facts.source: Pre-app 2026/03356/PA vs GPDO A.4/AA.2/B.2 and TCPA s.192

facts.topic: Composite/hybrid extension risk under PD
facts.detail: A single joined structure that is partly two-storey (3m) and partly single-storey (running to 8m) is vulnerable: A.1(g)/(f) require the enlarged part to 'have a single storey' for the 4m/8m depths, and A.1(ja) tests the joined total against (e)-(j) including the multi-storey limits in (h). Appeal decisions on hybrid enlarged parts are inconsistent. Safest maximising structure: single-storey PD run to 8m (prior approval), two-storey element delivered by planning permission (4m conceded), physically and procedurally distinct applications; alternatively build the 3m two-storey PD element and the single-storey run as separate sequential operations each certified by LDC — but take the planning 4m instead, it is deeper.
facts.source: GPDO A.1(f)/(g)/(h)/(ja); Planning Jungle LDC appeal-decision commentary

facts.topic: Site-specific checks before executing
facts.detail: (1) Rear garden depth ≥7m from the proposed two-storey back wall (A.1(h)(ii)) — if not, the 3m PD fallback fails and only the planning route delivers two-storey. (2) Height/eaves of the 2005 extension (must let the joined 8m total pass A.1(f)(ii)/(i)). (3) Conditions on S/03404/05/FUL (art.3(4) PD removal). (4) Whether the house predates 28 Oct 2018 and post-dates 1 July 1948 for Class AA (near-certain for a 1930s Kings Heath detached, but AA is unavailable if it is pre-1948). (5) No Article 4 direction / conservation area (Kings Heath — confirm not article 2(3) land, else A.1(g), AA and parts of B fall away). (6) Curtilage and original-footprint survey for the 50% cap.
facts.source: Derived from statutory limits applied to task site data

open_questions: Exact conditions on the 2005 permission S/03404/05/FUL — does any condition remove GPDO rights (art.3(4)/Dunnett test)?
Height and eaves height of the existing 2005 rear extension — does the joined 8m total pass A.1(f)(ii) (≤4m) and A.1(i) (eaves ≤3m within 2m of boundary)?
Distance from the proposed two-storey rear wall to the rear curtilage boundary — is the ≥7m rule in A.1(h)(ii) met?
Construction date of the dwellinghouse — after 1 July 1948 (Class AA gateway) and before 28 October 2018?

Is 115 Vicarage Road on article 2(3) land or subject to any Article 4 direction (Kings Heath has no conservation area at this address to my knowledge, but must be confirmed via Birmingham CC constraints mapping)?
Curtilage area and original house footprint (for the A.1(b) 50% computation, including the side wing's ground coverage and any outbuildings)
Is the two-storey flat-roof side extension original (pre-1948/as-built) or a later addition — affects A.1(ja) totals and side-width headroom under A.1(j)?

Precise in-force date and SI number of the Class B amendment permitting enlargements joining the original roof to an extension roof (understood to be SI 2024/579, 25 May 2024 — verify on legislation.gov.uk, which was proxy-blocked in this session)
